name: Curaçao

findings.controller: Not stated (cable supplier for the Curaçao landing not named in opened sources)
findings.local_actor: Aquatel / Qonèkt Telecom (Aqualectra group, Curaçao landing party) with SETAR N.V. and the Government of Curaçao
findings.financier: Government of Curaçao (budget allocation, Cg 44.6 million planned)
findings.summary: Aquatel, SETAR and the Curaçao government signed an agreement to land and operate the CELIA subsea cable (Florida–Caribbean) on Curaçao, reported at about US$27 million, targeting service by Q3 2027; government later earmarked Cg 44.6 million.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: equipment-vendor rule needs the cable supplier, and no opened source names one for the Curaçao segment; the Aruba record (ABW-002) codes ASN (France) as CELIA trunk supplier, which would make this third if the branch is ASN-supplied. Opened reports relay the same signing, so not treated as independent; no S1 opened. US$27m is DCD/SubTel's figure; Cg 44.6m (Nov 2025) not converted. Later SubTel item says Qonèkt Telecom began permitting for a Parasasa Beach landing; its date is inconsistent on-page (May 2025 byline vs May 2026 metadata), so recorded null. Not operational.

findings.controller: Blue NAP Americas (data-centre operator headquartered in Curaçao)
findings.local_actor: Blue NAP Americas; Government of Curaçao (partner, per minister's announcement)
findings.summary: Blue NAP Americas launched a GPU-based AI infrastructure-as-a-service platform at its Willemstad data centre with partners Radian Arc and Emerging International, reported as fully operational; the government presented it as the Caribbean's first sovereign AI platform.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator rule: Blue NAP Americas is Curaçao-headquartered (ownership undisclosed), so domestic. Radian Arc supplies the GPU stack; if it operates the GPUs it could be the controller of the compute (Radian Arc's home jurisdiction not stated in opened sources). GPU vendor and quantity not stated. The US$2m is called a joint partner investment by Developing Telecoms but a government investment by Curaçao Chronicle; unresolved. Tier 5 because reported operational, though scale appears small; reviewer may prefer a lower tier. Confidence medium, not high, given vague technical detail.
